title: 4/11 Hetzner deploy runs reported success while git pull failed (safe.directory) and the restart hit the wrong unit manager
tier_reason: the deploy path reported success without installing or restarting the pushed code, so a shipped fix would not have taken effect (deploy recoverability); the code actually stranded between 4/11 01:21 and the 4/12 11:52 ET run was dashboard cosmetics plus workflow and docs changes

contract.text: A successful deploy run installs the pushed commit on the box and restarts the production services on it.
contract.source: .github/workflows/deploy.yml at 51ef987 (git pull --ff-only; systemctl restart bts-scheduler bts-dashboard; echo 'Deployed <sha>')

mechanism.text: the workflow ran git pull as root in the bts-owned checkout without a safe.directory entry, so git refused the repository and the pull failed; with no set -e the script carried on, restarted services and the run concluded success

root's systemctl restart addressed the system-level manager, not the bts user's units that the operator treated as canonical (user-level units were created 4/11 22:04; legacy system-level units from the 01:08 setup were still present, I-020)

residual.text: the workflow still had no set -e, so any failing step kept reporting success until 6bffd63 on 4/14 (I-028)
the paths filter excluded .github/workflows/deploy.yml, so 870cede and cda8c1c triggered no run; they first ran with d5c466c on 4/12, and 8193909 added the workflow file to the filter
residual.source: deploy_runs.json (no run for 870cede or cda8c1c); 8193909 body

residual.text: restarting only the user-level units left the legacy system-level scheduler running until 8193909 (I-020)

watchdog.trigger: after a deploy run concludes success, the box's HEAD differs from the run's head SHA, or no scheduler (user unit) start is recorded after the run
watchdog.recovery_assertion: box HEAD equals the pushed SHA and a single scheduler process started after the run

evidence.what: 'fix(deploy): add safe.directory for git pull (was silently failing)'
root can't see user-level units without XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; 'Previous systemctl restart silently failed since the units only exist under the bts user's service manager'
the three Hetzner runs on 4/11 (05:21Z–06:14Z; heads d771ae1, 76b63fa, 17ca511) concluded success; logs expired
next run 2026-04-12T15:52:42Z (head d5c466c), the first whose workflow contained 870cede and cda8c1c; concluded success; log expired
system-level units were created by the original Hetzner setup at 01:08 on 4/11; user-level units at 22:04 on 4/11

notes: disposition changed from the lead row (UC) to observed_incident: 870cede's subject says the pull 'was silently failing', written within an hour of the three 4/11 runs; the alternative is unresolved_candidate pending the expired run logs (Phase 2 deploy_history.txt)

cda8c1c's diagnosis ('units only exist under the bts user's service manager') conflicts with 8193909's later finding that legacy system-level units existed; read together, root's restart reached the legacy units, not the user units
tier A reads 'loss of recoverability' as 'the deploy path silently did not take effect'; the lead may prefer B because nothing production-relevant was stranded

stranded code is inference from git history: only d771ae1, 76b63fa, 17ca511 (dashboard) and workflow/docs commits were pushed before the 4/12 run; whether the box was pulled by hand meanwhile is not evidenced
deployed: the fixes first ran in Hetzner run 24310493193; log expired
log bound: live by 2026-06-07T00:11:19Z (first_live_log sha eaccaf8)
